author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimony for the Church — No. 11 (the original pamphlet of the text later printed as 1T 486.2; its year comes from the 1T appendix note at 1T 717.6; the vision was Dec. 25, 1865, T11 40.1)
text: I was shown that the Health Reform is a part of the third angel’s message, and is just as closely connected with this message, as the arm and hand with the human body. I saw that we as a people must make an advance move in this great work. Ministers and people must act in concert. God’s people are not prepared for the loud cry of the third angel.
note: The 'arm and hand' statement in its original wording: health reform is part of the third angel's message and belongs to readiness for the loud cry.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimony for the Church — No. 12 (prints letters of May and June 1867, T12 91.1; pamphlet year not printed)
text: The Health Reform is closely connected with the work of the third message, yet it is not the message. Our preachers should teach the Health Reform, yet they should not make this the leading theme in the place of the message. Its place is among those subjects which set forth the preparatory work to meet the events brought to view by the message, among which it is prominent.
note: Limit on the claim: health reform is closely connected with the third message but 'is not the message'. It is preparatory work and never the leading theme.

author: Ellen G. White
work: “Christian Temperance” (address delivered in Battle Creek, March 6, 1869, reported by U. Smith), Testimony for the Church — No. 18
text: We are not our own. … But we have been purchased with a dear price. We have cost an immense sum, even the sufferings and death of the Son of God. If we can understand this, and fully realize it, then shall we feel great responsibility resting upon us to keep ourselves in the very best condition of health, that we may render to God perfect service.
note: 1 Cor 6:19-20 applied to health: a body bought by Christ's death is to be kept 'in the very best condition of health' for God's service.

author: James White
work: Bible Hygiene (a collection of James White's writings on hygiene, per the editor's note at BHY 163.1; dates of the originals not given)
text: The teachings of our Lord Jesus Christ and his holy apostles are in perfect accordance with the proposition that God, in all dispensations of probationary time, tests man just where he tested the innocent pair in Eden. … And the words of Paul, addressed to the Christian church, make proper eating and drinking a matter of grave importance: “Whether, therefore, ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.”
note: God tests man in every dispensation 'just where he tested the innocent pair in Eden'; set beside Luke 21:34 and 1 Cor 10:31, this makes eating and drinking 'a matter of grave importance'.

author: James White
work: Health, or, How to Live, No. 1, Introduction (signed “JAMES WHITE.”, HHTL 3.4)
text: We are deeply impressed with the great fact that grains and fruits are the proper food for man. These are best, and generally far the cheapest, which is a worthy consideration for the poor. Cheerful toil, or exercise, proper rest in sleep, air, water and light, are Heaven’s great remedies.
note: The 1865 baseline on diet and remedies: grains and fruits are man's proper food; exercise, sleep, air, water and light are 'Heaven's great remedies'.

author: A. T. Jones
work: “Health Reform by Faith,” The Home Missionary 5, no. 10, pp. 229-231 (November 1893); the editor's introduction calls it “a report of a talk on health reform given by Elder A. T. Jones, at the Lansing camp-meeting” (HOMI November 1893, page 229.1)
text: Health reform, as such, is to be practiced by faith in Christ. And when our people get to that place where they will live health reform by faith in Christ, then they will live righteousness by faith in Christ. Any one who does not live righteousness by faith in Christ, cannot live health reform as God has given it. One is just as really a matter of faith as the other.
note: Health reform is to be lived 'by faith in Christ', as righteousness by faith is: 'One is just as really a matter of faith as the other.' The same paragraph applies Rom 14:23 to eating and drinking.
